core_obligations: Reduce to one chart (proof lines 1872-1883): the question is local on X, so by the characterization of Zariski local quasi-separatedness one may assume an affine scheme U with a surjective quasi-compact separated etale morphism to X; the projections of R = U x_X U are then surjective, quasi-compact, separated, etale, hence quasi-finite with finite fibres.

Find an invariant open where the relation is finite (proof lines 1883-1894): at each generic point of an irreducible component of U there is an open neighbourhood over which the source projection becomes finite; finiteness descends along the etale cover, so the largest open W where that projection is finite is invariant; by construction W contains every generic point of an irreducible component.

Conclude (proof lines 1894-1902): the relation restricts to a relation R_W on W equal to the preimages of W under the two projections, and the projections are finite etale by construction; the open subspace X' = W/R_W of X induces a bijection on points of codimension zero, which reduces the statement to the finite etale case treated separately.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a single affine etale chart and record the properties of the two projections of the relation.
Use generic finiteness and invariance to produce an invariant open over which the relation is finite.
Pass to the quotient of that open and reduce to the finite etale case.
difficulty_reason: The proposition proves that a Zariski locally quasi-separated algebraic space contains a dense open subspace which is a scheme, containing every point of codimension zero (statement lines 1863-1870). The proof (proof lines 1872-1906) reduces to a single affine etale chart, uses generic finiteness, descent of finiteness and invariance of the locus of finiteness to produce an invariant open over which the relation is finite, and reduces the remaining statement to the finite etale case. H3: a three-stage reduction with a genuine invariance argument, written out in full.
